abstract: Census Bureau Business Trends and Outlook Survey, biweekly cycle 202621, published October 22, 2026. Question 7 asks whether a business used AI in any of its business functions in the last two weeks; Question 24 asks whether it expects to within six months. This is the first release published under Executive Order 14434, which directs agencies to use 'Super Intelligence' (SI) in place of 'Artificial Intelligence' (AI): Census relabelled both questions 'Super Intelligence or SI (formerly referred to as Artificial Intelligence or AI)' across the whole series without revising any value. This is the highest-frequency firm-side AI adoption measure in the US and the series jobsdata.ai plots on ai-adoption-rate, dated to reference-period end.
keyFindings: National AI use was 24.6 percent of firms (SE 0.27 percent) for the two weeks ending 2026-10-04, up from 23.8 percent for the cycle ending 2026-09-20 and the highest reading in the series.
The 0.8-point increase is about 1.6 standard errors of the difference, so it is suggestive rather than statistically significant on its own; it does resume the rise that paused in cycle 202620.
The six-month expectation (Q24) rose to 28.6 percent (SE 0.21 percent) from 27.7 percent, keeping the gap between expected and current use near 4 points.
Firms answering 'do not know' to current use held at 9.6 percent, so the gain came from fewer 'no' answers (65.8 percent, from 66.4 percent).

The relabel to 'Super Intelligence' is a terminology change under Executive Order 14434, which defines SI as the technologies covered by the statutory definition of artificial intelligence; no historical estimate changed.
methodology: Biweekly establishment survey of about 1.2 million US businesses split into six panels, each responding once every 12 weeks; published as an experimental data product. Cycle 202621 was collected 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-18 for the reference period 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-04 and published 18 days after the reference period ended. Per the Data Dictionary, responses were collected with the V4 core questionnaire, whose Q7 wording reads 'Artificial Intelligence (AI)'. The SI-worded questionnaires apply from cycle 202622 (with the SI supplement, current-use question moved to Q24) and from 202702 (core, with new Generative SI, headcount and new-hire questions at Q8-Q10). The November 2025 rewording to 'any business function' and the October 2026 relabel are both same-construct instrument changes; Census publishes one continuous series and so do we.
qualifiers: A firm-level adoption share, not a measure of how much work AI performs, and it counts any use in the prior two weeks. From cycle 202622 respondents see 'Super Intelligence' wording, a longer list of examples, and (in cycles 202622-202701) the question placed after the core economic items; any level shift at that point should be read as an instrument effect on the same construct, not a structural break. Executive Order 14434 asks for proposed legislation that may redefine SI; if the statutory definition changes, the construct question reopens. The Data Dictionary's questionnaire link points to an internal Census host that does not resolve publicly. The press releases are boilerplate; the National.xlsx workbook is the only reliable read.
